circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The facility represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit, following Bahrain and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street racing venue in Melbourne that encircles Albert Park Lake and hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, alongside various supporting racing series including the local Supercars Championship event. The track maintains FIA Grade 1 certification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, this 4. 326 km Austrian circuit originally opened as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix continuously from 1970 to 1987. After undergoing reconstruction and shortening, the track was renamed and subsequently hosted the Grand Prix again during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue on the Formula One calendar. Formula One racing began at the venue in 2016 with the European Grand Prix, before it became home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km track that hosted the first Formula One grand prix ever held in the Middle East. The venue, which holds FIA Grade 1 status, accommodates various racing series including GP2 and features multiple circuit configurations for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya is a 4. 657 km all-purpose racing venue featuring a balanced mix of straights and corners that test various driving skills. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Belgium's Spa-Francorchamps circuit, stretching over 7 km through the Walloon countryside near the town of Spa, has been a staple of international motorsport since hosting its inaugural Grand Prix in 1925. The venue became part of Formula One's inaugural season in 1950 and has maintained an unbroken presence on the calendar since 1985, aside from brief absences in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve spans 4. 361 kilometers and serves as the permanent home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its primary motorsport role, the venue has accommodated various international racing series including World Sportscar Championship events, open-wheel competitions, and multiple NASCAR categories throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport venue hosted the country's Formula One Grand Prix annually between 2004 and 2019, before resuming in 2024. The circuit has expanded its motorsport calendar to include electric racing events from 2024 onward.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing facility situated near Northamptonshire that became the venue for the inaugural 1948 British Grand Prix and subsequently hosted the first-ever World Championship race in 1950. Though the British Grand Prix alternated between three circuits during the mid-20th century, it has been a permanent fixture at Silverstone since 1987, which also stages MotoGP competitions.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km permanent circuit near Budapest, hosted Formula One's inaugural race behind the Iron Curtain in 1986. Originally intended as a street layout in the city's central park, the venue was instead constructed outside Budapest in just eight months, making it the fastest-built Formula One track to date.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale di Monza is a 5. 793 km track established in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. The venue has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949, making it one of only four circuits to remain on the Formula One calendar from the championship's inception, and earns its nickname "the Temple of Speed" from its distinctive layout featuring extended straights and fast-paced corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsport venue in Mie Prefecture, operated by Honda Mobilityland, with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is primarily recognized as a Formula One Grand Prix host and also features Japanese Super Formula racing events.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada near Las Vegas, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard alongside iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas. The track winds through urban streets featuring the city's premier hotels and casinos as key circuit elements.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez spans 4. 304 kilometers and honors two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents decades apart. The venue has returned to hosting the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, having previously staged the race during two earlier periods on a different configuration before 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Florida, stretching 3. 363 miles with 19 turns and an average qualifying speed near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it joined the championship calendar in 2022 and has since hosted the Miami Grand Prix annually.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco, commonly known as Monte Carlo, winds through the streets of the Principality's harbor district for 3. 337 kilometers, traversing both Monte Carlo and La Condamine neighborhoods. This street circuit remains one of motorsport's most iconic venues due to its tight urban layout.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after returning to Formula One in 2021 following a lengthy absence. The venue's partnership with the championship concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Located near Lusail in Qatar, this FIA Grade 1 circuit stretches 5. 419 kilometres with a prominent main straight spanning over one kilometre. The track is protected from desert sand by surrounding artificial grass, maintaining the racing surface in the arid environment.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, this 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit opened in 1940 and was later renamed after deceased racing driver José Carlos Pace in 1985. The venue hosts Formula One racing and features additional facilities including a karting track dedicated to another Brazilian motorsport legend.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Jeddah's waterfront in Saudi Arabia, where it has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since 2021. Located next to the Red Sea, the venue also began accommodating Formula E racing in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's downtown waterfront district, incorporating the urban areas of Downtown Core and Kallang into its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit combines extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One teams. The track accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators and holds the highest FIA safety classification.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility situated in Austin, Texas, hosting multiple major racing series including the Formula One United States Grand Prix, MotoGP, NASCAR, and the World Endurance Championship. Beyond its current events, the track has previously accommodated various motorsport competitions ranging from Australian touring cars to IndyCar racing.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver who currently represents Thailand in Formula One while driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having achieved two world championship titles with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond his single-seater success, Alonso has distinguished himself in endurance racing by winning the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, claiming two Le Mans 24-hour races with Toyota, and securing the Daytona 24-hour event in 2019, making him the sole driver to capture both Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli races for Mercedes in Formula One, having claimed eight Grand Prix victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for the Audi team after establishing himself through his racing career.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver competes for Cadillac in Formula One after achieving two consecutive runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while with Mercedes during 2019 and 2020. Across his 13-season career, Bottas has claimed 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan operates as a reserve driver for Haas in Formula One while actively competing in European Le Mans Series prototypes. He has appeared at seven Grand Prix events between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French driver, races for Alpine in Formula One. He achieved a Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020 during his time with AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One while driving for Red Bull Racing, bringing both French and Algerian heritage to the sport.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who has achieved a joint-record seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's tally. He holds multiple records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, notably winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand racing driver, currently competes in Formula One as a member of the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen competed in Formula One across two separate periods, from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he races for BMW's factory team WRT in the FIA World Endurance Championship while also pursuing a part-time NASCAR career with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, captured the 2025 Formula One World Championship with the team. Across his eight-season career, he has claimed 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The versatile competitor achieved his sole Grand Prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-season career. He finished as runner-up in the 2023 drivers' championship while driving for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell has secured eight victories across his Formula One career spanning eight seasons, currently competing for Mercedes in the championship.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his career spanning 12 seasons.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following previous involvement in IMSA's LMP2 division. He had a brief Formula One career spanning the 2023 and 2024 seasons.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the sport's top racing series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently holding a reserve position at both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. He competed as a full-time driver across five seasons from 2021 through 2025 before transitioning to a backup role in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has claimed four consecutive World Drivers' Championship titles between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, he has secured 73 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is the sole Chinese competitor to have raced in Formula One, having participated in the championship from 2022 through 2024. Currently, he holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the sport.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone since 2021, this French works team campaigns under the Alpine brand following Renault's rebranding strategy for the championship. The squad represented Renault's factory effort throughout the 2020s before the manufacturer's departure at season's end 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has engaged in Formula One racing through different organizational structures over time, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari and remains the sport's most enduring competitor, participating in every Formula One World Championship since the series' inaugural season in 1950. As the winningest team in the championship's history, Ferrari has become synonymous with Formula One excellence and carries the iconic nickname of "the Prancing Horse" among enthusiasts and analysts alike.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, the outfit commenced racing competition in the 2016 season. Ayao Komatsu assumed leadership as team principal in 2024, following the departure of Guenther Steiner, who held the position since the team's establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970 by Peter Sauber, built racing vehicles across multiple disciplines before joining Formula One in 1993. The constructor achieved notable success in endurance motorsport, including a Le Mans victory in 1989, but departed the grid in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving teams. Audi acquired the operation in 2024 to serve as the foundation for its forthcoming F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited represents one of Formula One's most established British outfits, operating from its Woking headquarters and currently fielding vehicles under corporate partnership arrangements. The organization functions as part of the broader McLaren Group structure, with majority ownership held by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a team operator and engine supplier, with the current incarnation, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, based in Brackley and holding a German licence. The team underwent a significant ownership restructuring in January 2022 when Ineos joined Mercedes-Benz Group and Toto Wolff as equal one-third stakeholders. Mercedes entries in the championship are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows".

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two teams under Red Bull's ownership, alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's second constructor entry in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that joined the grid in 2024, operating as the second team within Red Bull's F1 portfolio alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with a satellite facility in Milton Keynes, the squad represents Red Bull GmbH's expansion into fielding multiple competitive entries in the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England, has been a fixture in the sport since its 2005 establishment under the ownership of Red Bull GmbH. The squad operated under Christian Horner's management from its inception through 2024, with Laurent Mekies assuming the leadership role thereafter. As part of Red Bull's motorsport portfolio, the team competes alongside the separate Racing Bulls Formula One entry.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering Limited, founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Frank Williams's previous racing venture, represents one of Formula One's established British constructors. Headquartered at a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in the championship under the Atlassian Williams F1 Team banner as of 2026.
